known_defects: v1: 3 crossings. They are the nv-rms controller edges (e2/e3/e4) crossing the OOB trunk corridor (t1): the controller sits above the rail and the devices sit below it, so the two fans braid. This is the best of three measured layouts (7 -> 3) and no relation, group order or label was traded for it.
v1: 'client on LAN' (e1) and 'NVUE REST+gRPC' (e4) are role/protocol summaries, not literal protocol names; SSH/SFTP and legacy IPMI are abbreviated away.
v1: the trunk has two branch junctions plus a corridor terminus, not the single split point the source demands (see blockers).
v2: 'hosts FM?' is drawn dashed with a question mark because the excerpts never state the interface between the driver stack and Fabric Manager.

v2: the compute-host residency of Driver+CUDA, DCGM, dcgm-exporter and Fabric Mgr is carried by the view framing and the inband group colour, not by a printed label - the renderer draws group colours without a group-name legend, and no GPU-die node exists so no false 'on the die' claim is made.

Both views are static by design (the case requests no animation): dots are absent, so round-03 origin/synchronization lines read 0/0 and 0 synchronized at 2000ms - vacuously clean, not proven motion. The 5 captured frames are identical static frames proving content, not direction.

The in-pane viewport line reads 'viewport: unknown zoom: 1.00 natural' inside a live alternate-screen pane; the pane header proves the measured size and zoom ('77x47 @100%'), which is the evidence the validator accepts.
blockers: ONE-SPLIT OOB TRUNK: the source demands one arrow leaving the OOB LAN that splits in exactly one place into Compute BMC, NVSwitch BMC and Power shelf. The trunk primitive (id/label/from/to/branches) routes one corridor from `from` to `to` and gives every branch its own junction on that corridor, so a single split point is not expressible. v1 draws the honest closest shape - one bus, two branch junctions, corridor terminus at the third destination - and this blocker is recorded rather than presented as one split.
The renderer rejects a trunk whose branch is also its `to`, so the corridor must terminate at one of the destinations; there is no way to make all three destinations pure branch spurs.

nv-rms -> NVSwitch BMC is contested inside the source (line 283 lists the NVSwitch BMC as a rms device class and then says rms reaches the NVSwitch only through NVOS). No supervisor fact resolves it, so the edge is blocked rather than guessed.

abbreviations.NVUE REST+gRPC: 'NVUE REST, SSH/SFTP, and NMX-C gRPC' (line 283) compressed to fit the 14-character edge-label target; SSH/SFTP kept in the audit.
abbreviations.runs on K8s: 'Kubernetes' abbreviated for an edge label; the node label keeps the full word.
abbreviations.hosts FM?: 'Fabric Manager' abbreviated; the question mark plus dashed style marks the unconfirmed interface.
abbreviations.OOB drops: one label owning the whole trunk (corridor plus every spur), so no second ambiguous string is introduced.
